title: Transferring RL Gains from a Weaker Teacher
question: Supervising a student's own rollouts token by token, choose what to transfer from the teacher — its distribution, or the change reasoning tuning made to it.
elab:
On-policy distillation supervises a student on its own sampled tokens. A teacher's RL-tuning delta relative to its pre-RL reference can transfer useful reasoning even when the teacher is weaker than the student; this task designs that per-token signal for one weaker-teacher distillation run, scored on three held-out math benchmarks.

On-policy distillation trains a student on its own rollouts and supervises each token with a frozen teacher; the usual signal is the teacher's log-probability minus the student's. Recent work argues that is the wrong quantity — what should transfer is not the teacher's distribution but the change post-training made to it, visible by also holding the teacher's own pre-post-training base. The task asks for the per-token signal in the regime where that difference matters most: the teacher is weaker than the student (a small post-trained model teaching a larger one), so imitating the teacher pulls the student toward a worse model while its post-training delta can still help. One distillation run is scored on three held-out math benchmarks. It matters because on-policy distillation is now the standard way reasoning ability is moved between models, and the signal is its core.

description_md:
# Per-token training signal for on-policy distillation

## The question

On-policy distillation trains a student on **its own** rollouts and supervises
them token by token with a frozen teacher. The usual signal is the teacher's
log-probability of the sampled token minus the student's (T − S). A 2026 line of
work argues that this is the wrong quantity: what you want to transfer is not the
teacher's distribution but the *change* reasoning tuning made to it, which you
can see by also holding a frozen **reference** model — the checkpoint the teacher
was tuned from — and looking at the difference between the two (T − R).

This task is scoped to that second regime: **transferring the teacher's
post-training delta, T − R, where R is the teacher's own base.** The claim under
test is that the delta transfers reasoning even when the teacher is **not
stronger** than the student: it carries the change post-training made, not an
absolute teacher-vs-student comparison. A pure T − S signal, by contrast, is
classic distillation — it pulls the student toward the teacher itself, and only
helps when the teacher is the better model.

So in **every** setting the teacher is **weaker than the student**: a smaller
post-trained model, scored below the student on the held-out benchmarks, with
the frozen reference being that teacher's own pre-post-training base. A T − S
signal therefore pulls the student toward a worse model and is expected to land
at or near the do-nothing baseline, while a good delta signal should still
improve the student. The settings score the same distilled student on
different held-out problems of the domain it is trained on, one held-out
benchmark per setting.

Given the student's own rollout and what all three models assign to each
sampled token, **what per-token training signal built on the teacher's
post-training delta transfers reasoning best from a teacher that is weaker than
its student?**

That is the whole task. The rollout, the three forward passes, the PPO-clipped
policy-gradient update and the optimizer are fixed; you write the function that
turns the log-probabilities into the dense per-token advantage.

*Sibling task.* `llm-on-policy-distillation` is the regime-1 object — classic
on-policy distillation from a stronger teacher, a pure T − S signal over the full
logit surface. This task is the regime-2 object: the teacher is never stronger
than the student, the estimator is over the student's own sampled token (plus
top-K expectations), and it has the frozen reference model that regime-1 does
not. Keep the two distinct.

## Your surface

One function, in `opd2/src/open_r1/trainers/custom_token_signal.py`:

```python
def compute_per_token_signal(
    student_lp, teacher_lp, teacher_base_lp,
    mean_student_lp, mean_teacher_lp, mean_teacher_base_lp,
    completion_mask, solutions, step, total_steps,
) -> torch.Tensor:          # [B, T] float
```

All six tensors are `[B, T]` float32 on the same device, aligned to the
student's own sampled tokens. Writing `S`, `T`, `R` for the student, the
teacher and the frozen reference, all log-probabilities normalised over the
full vocabulary at the training temperature:

| argument | meaning |
|---|---|
| `student_lp` | `S(t) = log p_student(y_t \| prompt, y_<t)` at the token the student actually sampled |
| `teacher_lp` | `T(t)`, the same token under the frozen teacher |
| `teacher_base_lp` | `R(t)`, the same token under the frozen reference the teacher was tuned from |
| `mean_student_lp` | `E_{v~p_student}[ log p_student(v) ]` — the expectation is over the student's own next-token distribution, truncated to its top-K columns |
| `mean_teacher_lp` | `E_{v~p_student}[ log p_teacher(v) ]` |
| `mean_teacher_base_lp` | `E_{v~p_student}[ log p_reference(v) ]` |
| `completion_mask` | `[B, T]` bool. True on real sampled tokens; False on padding and on rollouts the harness has already rejected. Values at False positions are zeros and are discarded afterwards — but any reduction you take across tokens or across the batch has to respect it. |
| `solutions` | `list[str]`, length `B`: the **training** set's own reference answer for each prompt. Training data, not evaluation data. |
| `step`, `total_steps` | 0-based optimizer step and the total for this run, so a schedule is expressible. |

Return `[B, T]`, same shape as `student_lp`. Larger means *make this token more
likely*. Non-finite entries are zeroed for you. A wrong shape or a non-tensor
return raises rather than being silently coerced.

## Fixed, and not reachable from here

The rollout and its sampling parameters; the three frozen forward passes and
the top-K gather that produces the expectations; the PPO clip and the
ratio-vs-old-logprob machinery; the masking of padding and of degenerate
rollouts; the constant the signal is multiplied by before it enters the loss;
the optimizer, the learning-rate schedule, the step budget and the checkpoint
that is saved. The student and both frozen models are fixed. You cannot change
the state distribution — only what is said about the states the student visits.
The **gradient path** is fixed with it: this surface is a policy-gradient signal
over the student's own *sampled* tokens, not direct-backprop distribution
matching over the full vocabulary — a full-logit or teacher-top-K objective is a
different surface and lives in the sibling task `llm-distill-sgo-objective`.

## Reference baselines

The delta family, a pure-T−S baseline, and a null — expressed on exactly this
surface, ported from `naver-ai/opd2` at commit `2dac53fb` (Apache-2.0) and the
G-OPD paper below. The three delta-family arms are what a regime-2 contribution
must beat; they should all beat the null in every setting.

**delta_raw** — the raw RL-delta, T − R, at the sampled token: the teacher minus
its own pre-RL reference, no correction, no gating. The clean regime-2 anchor
(and the shipped starter). It is the delta term of OPD², before centring and
gating. Heo, Hwang, Yun & Han, *On-Policy Delta Distillation*, arXiv:2607.15161.

```python
return teacher_lp - teacher_base_lp
```

**ExOPD** — reward extrapolation past the teacher: scale the RL-delta by λ > 1
and subtract the student's own gap to the reference. Yang, Liu, Xie, Yang, Yang &
Lin, *Learning beyond Teacher: Generalized On-Policy Distillation with Reward
Extrapolation*, arXiv:2602.12125; λ = 1.25 is upstream's default, after
`src/open_r1/trainers/exopd_trainer.py`.

```python
lam = 1.25
return lam * (teacher_lp - teacher_base_lp) - (student_lp - teacher_base_lp)
```

**OPD²** — the delta signal, centred under the student's own distribution and
gated by the direction plain OPD would move. Heo et al., arXiv:2607.15161,
after `src/open_r1/trainers/opd2_trainer.py`.

```python
signal = (teacher_lp - teacher_base_lp) - (mean_teacher_lp - mean_teacher_base_lp)
d_base = (teacher_lp - student_lp)      - (mean_teacher_lp - mean_student_lp)
return torch.where((signal * d_base) < 0, torch.zeros_like(signal), signal)
```

**OPD (T − S) — not a delta-family method.** Plain on-policy
distillation: the teacher-minus-student log-prob at the sampled token, with no
reference model. This is classic distillation from a stronger teacher (the
regime-1 signal), included as a baseline: with a teacher weaker than the student
it has nothing better to pull toward, so it is expected to sit at or near the
do-nothing baseline and to lag the delta family. That is the point being
measured, not a defect. Heo et al., arXiv:2607.15161 ("OPD" column),
`src/open_r1/trainers/opd_trainer.py`.

```python
return teacher_lp - student_lp
```

**null** — a constant signal, carrying no teacher or reference information at
all. It reduces the fixed update to on-policy self-SFT (entropy minimisation on
the student's own rollouts), a strong self-improvement baseline on a capable
student; the delta family must beat it wherever the signal is real.

All are unrefereed 2026 preprints or simple baselines; treat their ordering as a
hypothesis to test, not as ground truth. The papers report the delta family
above a pure-T−S signal above the untouched student — but only with a teacher
stronger than the student, on students several times larger than the one here
and on a substantially larger training budget. The weaker-teacher direction
scored here is not one they run.

## Metric

Held-out accuracy of the distilled student, one held-out benchmark of the
reasoning domain it is trained on per setting; every setting scores the same
distilled student. Higher is better. What is measured is whether your per-token
signal transfers reasoning to unseen problems, not whether it was tuned to a
configuration you were handed.

"""Per-token training signal for on-policy distillation (EDITABLE).

The fixed pipeline samples a rollout from the student, then runs three frozen
forward passes over that rollout and hands you, for every sampled token, what
each model thinks of it.  Your job is to turn those numbers into the dense
per-token advantage the GRPO update is driven by.

Symbols used below (all log-probabilities, all at temperature `temperature`,
all normalised over the full vocabulary):

    S(t)   = log p_student(y_t | prompt, y_<t)     the student's own rollout
    T(t)   = log p_teacher(y_t | prompt, y_<t)     frozen reasoning-tuned teacher
    R(t)   = log p_reference(y_t | prompt, y_<t)   frozen model the teacher was tuned FROM

and the three expectations under the student's own next-token distribution,
truncated to the student's top-K columns (K is fixed by the harness):

    E[S](t) = sum_v p_student(v) * log p_student(v)
    E[T](t) = sum_v p_student(v) * log p_teacher(v)
    E[R](t) = sum_v p_student(v) * log p_reference(v)

What is fixed and NOT reachable from here: the rollout itself, the three
forward passes, the top-K gather, the PPO clip, the masking of padding and of
degenerate rollouts, the constant the signal is multiplied by before it enters
the loss, the optimizer, the schedule and the checkpoint that is saved.
"""
import torch


def compute_per_token_signal(
    student_lp: torch.Tensor,
    teacher_lp: torch.Tensor,
    teacher_base_lp: torch.Tensor,
    mean_student_lp: torch.Tensor,
    mean_teacher_lp: torch.Tensor,
    mean_teacher_base_lp: torch.Tensor,
    completion_mask: torch.Tensor,
    solutions: list,
    step: int,
    total_steps: int,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Return the dense per-token advantage for one batch of rollouts.

    Args:
        student_lp:           [B, T] float32, S(t).
        teacher_lp:           [B, T] float32, T(t).
        teacher_base_lp:      [B, T] float32, R(t).
        mean_student_lp:      [B, T] float32, E[S](t).
        mean_teacher_lp:      [B, T] float32, E[T](t).
        mean_teacher_base_lp: [B, T] float32, E[R](t).
        completion_mask:      [B, T] bool. True on real sampled tokens; False on
                              padding and on every position of a rollout the
                              harness has already rejected.  Values at False
                              positions are zeros and are discarded afterwards,
                              so you never have to mask your output -- but you
                              DO have to respect the mask in any reduction you
                              take across tokens or across the batch.
        solutions:            list[str] of length B, the training set's own
                              reference answer for each prompt.  Training data,
                              not evaluation data.
        step:                 optimizer step index, 0-based.
        total_steps:          total optimizer steps in this run.

    Returns:
        [B, T] float tensor, same shape as `student_lp`.  Larger means "make
        this token more likely".  Non-finite entries are zeroed by the harness.
    """
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # EDITABLE REGION
    #
    # Starter: the raw delta between the teacher and the model it was tuned
    # from, with no correction and no gating.  It is deliberately the crudest
    # form of the idea -- among other things it carries a nonzero mean offset,
    # so it pushes down on every token to some degree.
    delta = teacher_lp - teacher_base_lp
    return delta
    # END EDITABLE REGION
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

"""MLS-Bench fixed pipeline for the per-token-signal task (READ-ONLY).

Installed by vendor/pkg_configs/opd2/pre_edit.py.  Do not edit: the editable
surface is `custom_token_signal.compute_per_token_signal`.

Derived from naver-ai/opd2 @2dac53fb `src/open_r1/trainers/opd2_trainer.py`
(`OPD2Trainer._compute_opd_rewards`, Apache-2.0).  The three forwards, the
student top-K gather, the E_student[.] expectations, the invalid-row handling
and everything downstream are upstream's; only the line that builds the signal
is replaced by a call into the editable module.
"""
import logging
from typing import Optional

import torch

from .opd2_trainer import OPD2Trainer

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class MLSSignalTrainer(OPD2Trainer):
    """OPD2Trainer whose per-token signal comes from the editable module."""

    def _compute_opd_rewards(
        self,
        prompts_text,
        completion_ids: torch.Tensor,
        completion_mask: torch.Tensor,
        solutions,
        teacher_prompts_text=None,
    ) -> dict:
        # Imported per call so an ImportError or a SyntaxError in the editable
        # file surfaces with a traceback instead of a silent fallback.
        from .custom_token_signal import compute_per_token_signal

        args = self.opd_args
        device = self.accelerator.device
        tokenizer = self.processing_class
        B = len(prompts_text)
        T_max = completion_ids.size(1)

        rows = []          # per-rollout dicts of [T_i] tensors
        is_invalid_list = []

        base_model = self.model
        eval_model = self.opd_teacher_model
        tb_model = self.opd2_teacher_base_model

        with torch.no_grad():
            for idx in range(B):
                prompt_text = prompts_text[idx]
                comp_ids_row = completion_ids[idx]
                comp_mask_row = completion_mask[idx]

                # Every rank must run an identical number of forwards (ZeRO-3
                # all-gathers).  Invalid rows fall back to a length-1 forward
                # and are NaN'd downstream.  Upstream behaviour, unchanged.
                is_invalid = False
                valid_len = comp_mask_row.sum().item()
                if valid_len <= 1:
                    is_invalid = True
                    valid_len = max(valid_len, 1)
                comp_tokens = comp_ids_row[:valid_len]
                if len(comp_tokens) == 0:
                    is_invalid = True
                    comp_tokens = comp_ids_row[:1]
                comp_tensor = comp_tokens.unsqueeze(0)

                prompt_ids = tokenizer(
                    prompt_text, return_tensors="pt", add_special_tokens=False
                )["input_ids"].to(device)

                if teacher_prompts_text is not None:
                    teacher_prompt_ids = tokenizer(
                        teacher_prompts_text[idx], return_tensors="pt",
                        add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"].to(device)
                elif args.opd_no_think_mode and args.opd_no_think_teacher:
                    teacher_prompt_ids = tokenizer(
                        self._strip_nothink_block(prompt_text), return_tensors="pt",
                        add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"].to(device)
                else:
                    teacher_prompt_ids = prompt_ids

                reward_temp = self.temperature
                V_min = min(
                    self.accelerator.unwrap_model(base_model).config.vocab_size,
                    self.accelerator.unwrap_model(eval_model).config.vocab_size,
                    self.accelerator.unwrap_model(tb_model).config.vocab_size,
                )
                gt_ids = comp_tensor.clamp(max=V_min - 1).unsqueeze(-1)
                top_k = args.opd2_rewards_top_k
                K = min(top_k, V_min) if top_k > 0 else V_min

                base_gt, base_log_prob, topk_idx = self._forward_and_get_logp_topk(
                    base_model, prompt_ids, comp_tensor,
                    reward_temp=reward_temp, V_min=V_min, gt_ids=gt_ids, K=K)
                eval_gt, eval_log_prob, _ = self._forward_and_get_logp_topk(
                    eval_model, teacher_prompt_ids, comp_tensor,
                    reward_temp=reward_temp, V_min=V_min, gt_ids=gt_ids, topk_idx=topk_idx)
                tb_gt, tb_log_prob, _ = self._forward_and_get_logp_topk(
                    tb_model, teacher_prompt_ids, comp_tensor,
                    reward_temp=reward_temp, V_min=V_min, gt_ids=gt_ids, topk_idx=topk_idx)

                # E_{v ~ student}[ log p_*(v) ] over the student's top-K columns.
                # Kept in the log-probs' native dtype, exactly as upstream.
                base_prob = base_log_prob.exp()
                rows.append({
                    "student_lp": base_gt.squeeze(0),
                    "teacher_lp": eval_gt.squeeze(0),
                    "teacher_base_lp": tb_gt.squeeze(0),
                    "mean_student_lp": (base_prob * base_log_prob).sum(dim=-1).squeeze(0),
                    "mean_teacher_lp": (base_prob * eval_log_prob).sum(dim=-1).squeeze(0),
                    "mean_teacher_base_lp": (base_prob * tb_log_prob).sum(dim=-1).squeeze(0),
                })
                is_invalid_list.append(is_invalid)

        # ---- assemble the padded batch handed to the editable surface ------
        T_hook = max(1, max(r["student_lp"].shape[0] for r in rows))
        keys = ("student_lp", "teacher_lp", "teacher_base_lp",
                "mean_student_lp", "mean_teacher_lp", "mean_teacher_base_lp")
        batch = {k: torch.zeros(B, T_hook, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) for k in keys}
        hook_mask = torch.zeros(B, T_hook, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
        for i, r in enumerate(rows):
            L = r["student_lp"].shape[0]
            for k in keys:
                batch[k][i, :L] = r[k].to(torch.float32)
            if not is_invalid_list[i]:
                hook_mask[i, :L] = True

        step = int(getattr(self.state, "global_step", 0))
        total_steps = int(getattr(self.state, "max_steps", 0)
                          or getattr(self.args, "max_steps", 0) or 1)

        signal = compute_per_token_signal(
            student_lp=batch["student_lp"],
            teacher_lp=batch["teacher_lp"],
            teacher_base_lp=batch["teacher_base_lp"],
            mean_student_lp=batch["mean_student_lp"],
            mean_teacher_lp=batch["mean_teacher_lp"],
            mean_teacher_base_lp=batch["mean_teacher_base_lp"],
            completion_mask=hook_mask,
            solutions=list(solutions),
            step=step,
            total_steps=total_steps,
        )
        if not torch.is_tensor(signal):
            raise TypeError(
                "compute_per_token_signal must return a torch.Tensor of shape "
                f"[B, T] = [{B}, {T_hook}]; got {type(signal)!r}"
            )
        if tuple(signal.shape) != (B, T_hook):
            raise ValueError(
                "compute_per_token_signal returned shape "
                f"{tuple(signal.shape)}; expected [{B}, {T_hook}]"
            )
        signal = torch.nan_to_num(signal.detach().float(), nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)

        # ---- back to the [B, T_max] layout the fixed loss expects ----------
        signals_padded = torch.zeros(B, T_max, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
        signals_mask = torch.zeros(B, T_max, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
        for i, r in enumerate(rows):
            if is_invalid_list[i]:
                continue
            L = min(r["student_lp"].shape[0], T_max)
            signals_padded[i, :L] = signal[i, :L]
            signals_mask[i, :L] = True
        invalid = torch.tensor(is_invalid_list, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)

        self._log_reward_summary(signals_padded, signals_mask, invalid, completion_mask)

        if self.accelerator.is_main_process:
            _m = signals_mask.float()
            _n = _m.sum().clamp(min=1.0)
            _mean = float((signals_padded * _m).sum() / _n)
            _sq = float((signals_padded.pow(2) * _m).sum() / _n)
            print(
                f"TRAIN_METRICS step={step} total_steps={total_steps} "
                f"signal_mean={_mean:.6f} signal_rms={max(_sq, 0.0) ** 0.5:.6f} "
                f"tokens={int(signals_mask.sum())} invalid={int(invalid.sum())}",
                flush=True,
            )

        return {"signals": signals_padded, "mask": signals_mask, "invalid": invalid}

"""OPD Trainer: stripped-down OPDPO with only the core teacher-vs-student
log-prob-diff per-token reward.

per_token_signal = eval_gt - base_gt   (raw log-prob diff at the sampled token)

Differences vs OPDPOTrainer:
  - reward formula reduced to (eval_gt - base_gt), no mean correction / KL term
  - reward forward temperature is `self.temperature` (no separate opdpo_reward_temperature)
  - no tokenizer alignment with teacher (teacher must share vocab w/ student)
  - no perturb / multi-turn / use_answer_for_rollout
  - no top-K vocab gather
  - no per-token scale / clip / percentile-clamp
  - no γ-discount future spread (γ=0): raw per-token signal
  - no gamma_kl / use_gamma_kl / zero-mean
  - no ref_kl_mode surrogate
  - disable_adv_norm is always True (advantages = rewards, no group normalization)
"""

class _StepSkipCallback(TrainerCallback):
    """Skip the optimizer step when KL exceeds threshold (synchronized across ranks)."""

    def __init__(self, trainer: "OPDTrainer"):
        self.trainer = trainer

    def on_pre_optimizer_step(self, args, state, control, **kwargs):
        self.trainer._maybe_skip_step()

    def on_step_end(self, args, state, control, **kwargs):
        self.trainer._step_kl_microbatches = []


class OPDTrainer(GRPOTrainer):
    """GRPOTrainer subclass: per-token reward = (eval_gt - base_gt) - E_base[eval_logp - base_logp]."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        model,
        args: Optional[OPDConfig] = None,
        processing_class=None,
        **kwargs,
    ):
        def _opd_placeholder_reward(prompts, completions, completion_ids, **kw):

        _opd_placeholder_reward.__name__ = "opd_reward"

        kwargs.pop("reward_funcs", None)

        super().__init__(
            model=model,
            reward_funcs=[_opd_placeholder_reward],
            args=args,
            processing_class=processing_class,
            **kwargs,
        )

        self.opd_args = args

        # Route trl's vLLM-server broadcast_object_list over gloo (CPU) to avoid NCCL
        # transport corruption of the generation payload. Collective; all ranks call it.

        install_gloo_object_broadcast(is_main=self.accelerator.is_main_process)

        # Qwen3 + DeepSpeed can produce NaN logits during generation.
        if hasattr(self, "generation_config") and self.generation_config is not None:
            self.generation_config.renormalize_logits = True

        self._eta_start_time = None
        self._eta_step_count = 0

        self.opd_teacher_model: Optional[torch.nn.Module] = None
        # Teacher tokenizer: loaded only for opd_teacher_template (its chat_template
        # renders the teacher prompt; encoding still uses the student tokenizer since
        # OPD assumes a shared vocab).
        self.opd_teacher_tokenizer = None
        if args.opd_teacher:
            self._load_teacher_model(args.opd_teacher)
            if getattr(args, "opd_teacher_template", False):

                                f"{args.opd_teacher} (model_type={teacher_mt})",
                                flush=True,
                            )
                    except Exception as e:  # template rendering is opt-in; fail loudly
                        raise RuntimeError(
                            f"opd_teacher_template=True but teacher tokenizer load failed: {e}"
                        )

        self._step_kl_microbatches: list[float] = []
        self._step_skip_count: int = 0
        if args.opd_skip_kl_thres > 0:
            self._install_step_skip_hooks()

        if args.opd_no_think_mode and args.opd_only_think_mode:

                "opd_no_think_mode and opd_only_think_mode are mutually exclusive; "

        elif args.opd_only_think_mode:

    def _install_step_skip_hooks(self) -> None:
        self.add_callback(_StepSkipCallback(self))
        if self.accelerator.is_main_process:
            print(
                f"  [step skip] enabled: kl_thres={self.opd_args.opd_skip_kl_thres}",
                flush=True,
            )

    # ── no-think mode (Qwen-family chat_template patch) ──────────────────────
    _NOTHINK_OLD_SNIPPET = (
        "{%- if enable_thinking is defined and enable_thinking is false %}\n"
        "        {{- '<think>\\n\\n</think>\\n\\n' }}\n"
        "    {%- endif %}"
    )
    _NOTHINK_NEW_SNIPPET = "{{- '<think>\\n\\n</think>\\n\\n' }}"
    _NOTHINK_BLOCK = "<think>\n\n</think>\n\n"
    # only-think mode: open a thinking block with NO closing tag (force think on)
    _ONLYTHINK_NEW_SNIPPET = "{{- '<think>\\n' }}"

    # ── Gemma4 think-mode (pin `enable_thinking` at the template level) ──────
    # Gemma4 templates gate thinking on the `enable_thinking` kwarg (default OFF —
    # opposite of Qwen). Pinning the conditions makes the chosen mode the template
    # DEFAULT, so rollouts, the teacher render (opd_teacher_template), and any
    # downstream loader (evalchemy) all agree without passing kwargs.
    # ── PRE-2026-07-15 layout ("inline" form) ────────────────────────────────
    # Every use site re-tested the kwarg: `enable_thinking is defined and ...`.
    # NOTE: outer contains inner as a substring — replace outer FIRST.
    _G4_COND_OUTER = "(enable_thinking is defined and enable_thinking)"
    _G4_COND_INNER = "enable_thinking is defined and enable_thinking"
    # 31B-it only: default no-think guard that force-closes an empty thought
    # channel (`<|channel>thought\n<channel|>`) in the generation prompt.
    _G4_GUARD = "not enable_thinking | default(false)"

    # ── 2026-07-15+ layout ("normalized" form) ───────────────────────────────
    # Google's canonical template (hub commits E4B-it 6ea8ce9dfc86 / 31B-it
    # 68abe48010cb, "fix: chat template — null handling, reasoning preservation")
    # normalizes the flag ONCE at the top and then reads the bare name:
    #     {%- set enable_thinking = enable_thinking | default(false) -%}
    #     {%- if enable_thinking or tools or ... -%}   /   {%- if enable_thinking -%}
    #     {%- if not enable_thinking -%}   (31B thought-close guard)
    # None of the inline literals above survive that refactor, so pinning the
    # `set` line alone is both sufficient (all use sites read the normalized
    # variable) and safer than per-site substitution.
    _G4_SET_DEFAULT = "{%- set enable_thinking = enable_thinking | default(false) -%}"

    @staticmethod
    def _is_gemma4_template(tpl: str) -> bool:
        return "enable_thinking" in tpl and "<|turn>" in tpl

    @classmethod
    def _gemma4_pin_think_template(cls, tpl: str, tag: str) -> str:
        """Pin a Gemma4 chat template to only_think (enable_thinking=true: system
        turn opens with `<|think|>`, 31B thought-close guard disabled) or no_think
        (enable_thinking=false: no `<|think|>`, 31B guard always closes an empty
        thought channel). Handles both the pre-07-15 inline form and the 07-15+
        normalized form. Idempotent: the pinned literals no longer match.

        Raises RuntimeError when the template looks like Gemma4 but nothing could
        be pinned — a silent no-op here trains/evaluates in the WRONG think mode
        (this is exactly what broke the 2026-07-30 ge4b runs), so fail loudly
        instead of logging success.
        """
        on = tag == "only_think"
        orig = tpl
        # 07-15+ normalized form: one substitution covers every use site.
        tpl = tpl.replace(
            cls._G4_SET_DEFAULT,
            f"{{%- set enable_thinking = {'true' if on else 'false'} -%}}",
        )
        # pre-07-15 inline form (outer before inner: outer contains inner).
        tpl = tpl.replace(cls._G4_COND_OUTER, "true" if on else "false")
        tpl = tpl.replace(cls._G4_COND_INNER, "true" if on else "false")
        tpl = tpl.replace(cls._G4_GUARD, "false" if on else "true")
        if tpl == orig and not cls._gemma4_is_pinned(orig, tag):
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"[{tag}] Gemma4 chat_template matched no known enable_thinking "
                "layout — refusing to continue with an unpinned template. The "
                "upstream template probably changed again; add its form to "
                "_gemma4_pin_think_template. Template head: "
                f"{orig[:200]!r}"
            )
        return tpl

    @classmethod
    def _gemma4_is_pinned(cls, tpl: str, tag: str) -> bool:
        """True when `tpl` is already pinned to `tag` (makes the pin idempotent
        without tripping the no-op guard on a second pass)."""
        want = "true" if tag == "only_think" else "false"
        return (
            f"{{%- set enable_thinking = {want} -%}}" in tpl
            or "enable_thinking" not in tpl  # inline form: literals fully folded
        )

    @classmethod
    def _strip_nothink_block(cls, text: str) -> str:
        if text.endswith(cls._NOTHINK_BLOCK):
            return text[: -len(cls._NOTHINK_BLOCK)]
        return text

    def _patch_chat_template_no_think(self) -> None:
        self._patch_chat_template_think("no_think", self._NOTHINK_NEW_SNIPPET)

    def _patch_chat_template_only_think(self) -> None:
        self._patch_chat_template_think("only_think", self._ONLYTHINK_NEW_SNIPPET)

    def _patch_chat_template_think(self, tag: str, new_snippet: str) -> None:
        tok = self.processing_class
        if tok is None or not getattr(tok, "chat_template", None):
            if self.accelerator.is_main_process:
                print(f"  [{tag}] no chat_template found; skipping patch", flush=True)
            return
        if self._NOTHINK_OLD_SNIPPET not in tok.chat_template:
            # Gemma4 branch: pin enable_thinking on the student template, and on the
            # teacher tokenizer too when it was loaded (opd_teacher_template).
            if self._is_gemma4_template(tok.chat_template):
                tok.chat_template = self._gemma4_pin_think_template(tok.chat_template, tag)
                # Teacher must render in the SAME mode: with opd_teacher_template the
                # teacher's own template builds its prompts, so an unpinned teacher
                # silently misaligns teacher/student renders. Track whether it was
                # actually pinned — never claim "(+teacher)" just because one loaded.
                ttok = getattr(self, "opd_teacher_tokenizer", None)
                teacher_pinned = False
                if ttok is not None and getattr(ttok, "chat_template", None):
                    if self._is_gemma4_template(ttok.chat_template):
                        ttok.chat_template = self._gemma4_pin_think_template(
                            ttok.chat_template, tag
                        )
                        teacher_pinned = True
                if self.accelerator.is_main_process:
                    if ttok is not None and not teacher_pinned:
                        note = " (teacher NOT pinned — non-Gemma4 template?)"
                    elif teacher_pinned:
                        note = " (+teacher)"
                    else:
                        note = ""
                    print(
                        f"  [{tag}] gemma4 chat_template pinned in-memory{note}",
                        flush=True,
                    )
                return
            if self.accelerator.is_main_process:
                print(
                    f"  [{tag}] expected Qwen-family conditional not found in "
                    "chat_template; skipping patch (template unchanged)",
                    flush=True,
                )
            return
        tok.chat_template = tok.chat_template.replace(
            self._NOTHINK_OLD_SNIPPET, new_snippet
        )
        if self.accelerator.is_main_process:
            print(f"  [{tag}] chat_template patched in-memory", flush=True)

    def _force_patch_tokenizer_config_on_disk(self, output_dir: str, new_snippet: str, tag: str) -> None:
        import json
        import os
        cfg_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "tokenizer_config.json")
        if not os.path.exists(cfg_path):
            return
        try:
            with open(cfg_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                cfg = json.load(f)
        except Exception as e:
            if self.accelerator.is_main_process:
                print(f"  [{tag}] could not read {cfg_path}: {e}", flush=True)
            return
        tpl = cfg.get("chat_template")
        if not isinstance(tpl, str):
            return
        if self._NOTHINK_OLD_SNIPPET in tpl:
            cfg["chat_template"] = tpl.replace(
                self._NOTHINK_OLD_SNIPPET, new_snippet
            )
            with open(cfg_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(cfg, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
            if self.accelerator.is_main_process:
                print(f"  [{tag}] force-patched {cfg_path}", flush=True)

    def _force_patch_gemma4_template_on_disk(self, output_dir: str, tag: str) -> None:
        """Persist the pinned Gemma4 think mode into the checkpoint so any loader
        (evalchemy, vLLM) renders the same mode by default. Gemma4 keeps its
        template in chat_template.jinja; tokenizer_config.json / chat_template.json
        are covered as fallbacks. Idempotent (no-op once pinned)."""
        import json
        import os

        jinja_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "chat_template.jinja")
        if os.path.exists(jinja_path):
            try:
                with open(jinja_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    tpl = f.read()
                if self._is_gemma4_template(tpl):
                    new = self._gemma4_pin_think_template(tpl, tag)
                    if new != tpl:
                        with open(jinja_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                            f.write(new)
                        if self.accelerator.is_main_process:
                            print(f"  [{tag}] force-patched {jinja_path}", flush=True)
            except Exception as e:
                if self.accelerator.is_main_process:
                    print(f"  [{tag}] could not patch {jinja_path}: {e}", flush=True)

        for fname in ("tokenizer_config.json", "chat_template.json"):
            cfg_path = os.path.join(output_dir, fname)
            if not os.path.exists(cfg_path):
                continue
            try:
                with open(cfg_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    cfg = json.load(f)
                tpl = cfg.get("chat_template")
                if isinstance(tpl, str) and self._is_gemma4_template(tpl):
                    new = self._gemma4_pin_think_template(tpl, tag)
                    if new != tpl:
                        cfg["chat_template"] = new
                        with open(cfg_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                            json.dump(cfg, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
                        if self.accelerator.is_main_process:
                            print(f"  [{tag}] force-patched {cfg_path}", flush=True)
            except Exception as e:
                if self.accelerator.is_main_process:
                    print(f"  [{tag}] could not patch {cfg_path}: {e}", flush=True)

    def _save(self, output_dir=None, state_dict=None):
        super()._save(output_dir=output_dir, state_dict=state_dict)
        if output_dir is not None:
            if self.opd_args.opd_no_think_mode:
                self._force_patch_tokenizer_config_on_disk(
                    output_dir, self._NOTHINK_NEW_SNIPPET, "no_think")
                self._force_patch_gemma4_template_on_disk(output_dir, "no_think")
            elif self.opd_args.opd_only_think_mode:
                self._force_patch_tokenizer_config_on_disk(
                    output_dir, self._ONLYTHINK_NEW_SNIPPET, "only_think")
                self._force_patch_gemma4_template_on_disk(output_dir, "only_think")
        # Multimodal checkpoints (Gemma3): copy processor config JSONs from the base
        # model so vLLM can load the checkpoint. No-op for text-only models (Qwen).
        from open_r1.utils.model_utils import restore_missing_base_tensors, save_processor_configs
        out = output_dir if output_dir is not None else self.args.output_dir
        base_id = getattr(self.model.config, "_name_or_path", None)
        if out and base_id:
            save_processor_configs(base_id, out)
            # Gemma4 E4B: HF omits KV-shared layers' k/v_proj from the save but
            # vLLM requires them; restore base copies. No-op when keys match.
            if self.accelerator.is_main_process:
                restore_missing_base_tensors(base_id, out)

    def _maybe_skip_step(self) -> None:
        args = self.opd_args
        reasons: list[str] = []
        if args.opd_skip_kl_thres > 0 and self._step_kl_microbatches:
            local_kl = sum(self._step_kl_microbatches) / max(len(self._step_kl_microbatches), 1)
            kl_t = torch.tensor([local_kl], device=self.accelerator.device, dtype=torch.float32)
            global_kl = gather(kl_t).mean().item()
            if global_kl > args.opd_skip_kl_thres:
                reasons.append(f"KL={global_kl:.4f}>{args.opd_skip_kl_thres}")
        if not reasons:
            return
        for p in self.model.parameters():
            if p.grad is not None:
                p.grad.detach().zero_()
        self._step_skip_count += 1
        if self.accelerator.is_main_process:
            step = self.state.global_step if hasattr(self, "state") else -1
            print(
                f"  [SKIP step #{step}] " + ", ".join(reasons)
                + f" (total skips so far: {self._step_skip_count})",
                flush=True,
            )

    def _load_teacher_model(self, model_id_or_path: str) -> None:
        """Frozen teacher: stage-0 under ZeRO ≤ 2, sharded under ZeRO-3.

        Auto-detects FP8-quantized checkpoints via HF config.quantization_config
        and keeps native FP8 weights (no DeepSpeed wrap).
        """
        from transformers import AutoConfig
        from trl.models import prepare_deepspeed

        from open_r1.utils.model_utils import load_causal_lm

        main_unwrapped = self.accelerator.unwrap_model(self.model)
        main_dtype = next(main_unwrapped.parameters()).dtype

        is_fp8 = False
        try:
            cfg = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(model_id_or_path)
            qcfg = getattr(cfg, "quantization_config", None)
            if isinstance(qcfg, dict):
                qm = (qcfg.get("quant_method") or "").lower()
                if "fp8" in qm or qcfg.get("activation_scheme") is not None:
                    is_fp8 = True
            elif qcfg is not None and "fp8" in str(qcfg).lower():
                is_fp8 = True
        except Exception:
            pass

        if self.accelerator.is_main_process:
            print(
                f"  [opd_teacher] loading teacher model: {model_id_or_path} "
                f"(fp8={is_fp8}, main_dtype={main_dtype})",
                flush=True,
            )

        # load_causal_lm auto-handles multimodal checkpoints (e.g. Gemma3-27B teacher):
        # loads text-only, keeps vLLM-compatible param names, mirrors vocab_size.
        teacher = load_causal_lm(
            model_id_or_path,
            torch_dtype="auto" if is_fp8 else main_dtype,
        )
        teacher.eval()
        for p in teacher.parameters():
            p.requires_grad_(False)

        deepspeed_plugin = AcceleratorState().deepspeed_plugin
        force_z3 = bool(self.opd_args.opd_teacher_zero3)
        wrap_kind = "replicated"
        if is_fp8:
            if force_z3 and self.accelerator.is_main_process:
                print(
                    "  [opd_teacher] WARNING: opd_teacher_zero3=True ignored "
                    "for FP8 model (stage-3 incompatible with block-FP8 weights)",
                    flush=True,
                )
            teacher = teacher.to(self.accelerator.device)
            teacher = self.accelerator.prepare_model(teacher, evaluation_mode=True)
        elif deepspeed_plugin is not None:
            if force_z3:
                teacher = self._prepare_teacher_stage3(teacher, deepspeed_plugin)
                wrap_kind = "ZeRO-3 (forced)"
            else:
                teacher = prepare_deepspeed(teacher, self.accelerator)
                wrap_kind = "ZeRO via main plugin"
        else:
            teacher = self.accelerator.prepare_model(teacher, evaluation_mode=True)

        self.opd_teacher_model = teacher

        if self.accelerator.is_main_process:
            n_params = sum(p.numel() for p in teacher.parameters())
            print(
                f"  [opd_teacher] loaded: {n_params/1e9:.2f}B params"
                f"{' (FP8 native)' if is_fp8 else ''} [{wrap_kind}]",
                flush=True,
            )

    def _prepare_teacher_stage3(self, model, deepspeed_plugin) -> torch.nn.Module:
        import deepspeed
        from copy import deepcopy

        config_kwargs = deepcopy(deepspeed_plugin.deepspeed_config)
        hidden_size = (
            max(model.config.hidden_sizes)
            if getattr(model.config, "hidden_sizes", None)
            else getattr(model.config, "hidden_size", None)
        )
        zero_opt = config_kwargs.setdefault("zero_optimization", {})
        zero_opt["stage"] = 3
        if hidden_size is not None:
            zero_opt["reduce_bucket_size"] = hidden_size * hidden_size
            zero_opt["stage3_param_persistence_threshold"] = 10 * hidden_size
            zero_opt["stage3_prefetch_bucket_size"] = int(0.9 * hidden_size * hidden_size)
        model, *_ = deepspeed.initialize(model=model, config=config_kwargs)
        model.eval()
        return model

    def _get_per_token_logps(self, model, input_ids, attention_mask, logits_to_keep, batch_size=None) -> torch.Tensor:
        batch_size = batch_size or input_ids.size(0)
        all_logps = []
        for i in range(0, input_ids.size(0), batch_size):
            input_ids_batch = input_ids[i : i + batch_size]
            attention_mask_batch = attention_mask[i : i + batch_size]

            logits = model(
                input_ids=input_ids_batch, attention_mask=attention_mask_batch, logits_to_keep=logits_to_keep + 1
            ).logits
            logits = logits[:, :-1, :]
            input_ids_batch = input_ids_batch[:, -logits_to_keep:]
            logits = logits[:, -logits_to_keep:]
            logits.div_(self.temperature)
            if self.opd_args.opd_logit_fp32:
                logits = logits.float()
            logps = selective_log_softmax(logits, input_ids_batch)
            all_logps.append(logps)
        return torch.cat(all_logps, dim=0)

    def compute_loss(self, model, inputs, return_outputs=False, num_items_in_batch=None):
        if return_outputs:
            raise ValueError("The OPDTrainer does not support returning outputs")
        return self._compute_loss(model, inputs)

    def _compute_loss(self, model, inputs):
        """GRPO PPO-clipped loss with k3 pathwise KL gradient. advantages: [N, L] dense."""
        prompt_ids, prompt_mask = inputs["prompt_ids"], inputs["prompt_mask"]
        completion_ids, completion_mask = inputs["completion_ids"], inputs["completion_mask"]
        input_ids = torch.cat([prompt_ids, completion_ids], dim=1)
        attention_mask = torch.cat([prompt_mask, completion_mask], dim=1)
        logits_to_keep = completion_ids.size(1)

        per_token_logps = self._get_per_token_logps(
            model, input_ids, attention_mask, logits_to_keep
        )

        if self.beta != 0.0:
            with torch.no_grad():
                if self.ref_model is not None:
                    ref_per_token_logps = self._get_per_token_logps(
                        self.ref_model, input_ids, attention_mask, logits_to_keep
                    )
                else:
                    with self.accelerator.unwrap_model(self.model).disable_adapter():
                        ref_per_token_logps = self._get_per_token_logps(
                            self.model, input_ids, attention_mask, logits_to_keep
                        )
            per_token_kl = (
                torch.exp(ref_per_token_logps - per_token_logps) - (ref_per_token_logps - per_token_logps) - 1
            )

        advantages = inputs["advantages"]
        if advantages.dim() == 1:
            advantages = advantages.unsqueeze(1)

        _old = inputs.get("old_per_token_logps")
        old_per_token_logps = per_token_logps.detach() if _old is None else _old
        coef_1 = torch.exp(per_token_logps - old_per_token_logps)
        coef_2 = torch.clamp(coef_1, 1 - self.epsilon_low, 1 + self.epsilon_high)

        if self.args.delta is not None:
            coef_1 = torch.clamp(coef_1, max=self.args.delta)

        per_token_loss1 = coef_1 * advantages
        per_token_loss2 = coef_2 * advantages
        per_token_loss = -torch.min(per_token_loss1, per_token_loss2)
        per_token_loss = torch.nan_to_num(per_token_loss, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)

        # vLLM↔HF logprob mismatch correction. Mirrors GRPOTrainer.compute_loss
        # (trl 1.4 grpo_trainer.py:2560). When use_vllm=True, the sampled tokens
        # come from vLLM's distribution while old_per_token_logps is HF's logp at
        # those same tokens. Without this correction, tail tokens that vLLM picked
        # but HF rates low get full gradient weight, blowing up gn.
        if self.use_vllm and self.vllm_importance_sampling_correction:
            is_ratio = inputs.get("importance_sampling_ratio")
            if is_ratio is not None:
                per_token_loss = per_token_loss * is_ratio

        if self.beta != 0.0:
            per_token_loss = per_token_loss + self.beta * per_token_kl

        mode = "train" if self.model.training else "eval"
        # trl 1.4 GRPOTrainer.compute_loss bypasses Trainer.training_step's ga scaling
        # (via the compute_loss_func="non-None ..." hack in super().__init__). We
        # override compute_loss with our own _compute_loss, so we must do the
        # gradient_accumulation_steps division here ourselves to match trl's pattern.
        if self.loss_type == "grpo":
            loss = ((per_token_loss * completion_mask).sum(-1) / completion_mask.sum(-1).clamp(min=1.0)).mean()
            normalizer = self.current_gradient_accumulation_steps if mode == "train" else 1.0
            loss = loss / normalizer
        elif self.loss_type == "bnpo":
            loss = (per_token_loss * completion_mask).sum() / completion_mask.sum().clamp(min=1.0)
            normalizer = self.current_gradient_accumulation_steps if mode == "train" else 1.0
            loss = loss / normalizer
        elif self.loss_type == "dr_grpo":
            loss = (per_token_loss * completion_mask).sum() / (per_token_loss.size(0) * self.max_completion_length)
            normalizer = self.current_gradient_accumulation_steps if mode == "train" else 1.0
            loss = loss / normalizer
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown loss type: {self.loss_type}")

        if self.beta != 0.0:
            mean_kl = (per_token_kl * completion_mask).sum() / completion_mask.sum().clamp(min=1.0)
            self._metrics[mode]["kl"].append(self.accelerator.gather(mean_kl).nanmean().item())
            if self.opd_args.opd_skip_kl_thres > 0 and self.model.training:
                self._step_kl_microbatches.append(float(mean_kl.detach().item()))

        is_low_clipped = (coef_1 < 1 - self.epsilon_low) & (advantages < 0)
        is_high_clipped = (coef_1 > 1 + self.epsilon_high) & (advantages > 0)
        is_region_clipped = is_low_clipped | is_high_clipped

        low_clip = (is_low_clipped * completion_mask).sum() / completion_mask.sum().clamp(min=1.0)
        high_clip = (is_high_clipped * completion_mask).sum() / completion_mask.sum().clamp(min=1.0)
        clip_ratio = (is_region_clipped * completion_mask).sum() / completion_mask.sum().clamp(min=1.0)

        gathered_low_clip = self.accelerator.gather(low_clip)
        self._metrics[mode]["clip_ratio/low_mean"].append(gathered_low_clip.nanmean().item())
        self._metrics[mode]["clip_ratio/low_min"].append(nanmin(gathered_low_clip).item())
        gathered_high_clip = self.accelerator.gather(high_clip)
        self._metrics[mode]["clip_ratio/high_mean"].append(gathered_high_clip.nanmean().item())
        self._metrics[mode]["clip_ratio/high_max"].append(nanmax(gathered_high_clip).item())
        gathered_clip_ratio = self.accelerator.gather(clip_ratio)
        self._metrics[mode]["clip_ratio/region_mean"].append(gathered_clip_ratio.nanmean().item())

        return loss

    @staticmethod
    def _group_normalize(
        x: torch.Tensor,
        valid_mask: torch.Tensor,
        N: int,
        G: int,
        T: int,
        mean_only: bool = False,
    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """Per-GRPO-group zero-mean (and /std unless mean_only) over G×T valid tokens.
        Used for metric tracking only (advantages = raw rewards in OPD)."""
        g = x.view(N, G, T).float()
        v = valid_mask.view(N, G, T).float()
        total_valid = v.sum(dim=(1, 2))
        mean = (g * v).sum(dim=(1, 2)) / total_valid.clamp(min=1)
        diff = (g - mean.view(N, 1, 1)) * v
        std = (diff.pow(2).sum(dim=(1, 2)) / (total_valid - 1).clamp(min=1)).sqrt()
        std = torch.where(total_valid <= 1, torch.zeros_like(std), std)
        mean = torch.where(total_valid == 0, torch.zeros_like(mean), mean)
        mean_t = mean.view(N, 1, 1).expand(N, G, T).reshape(x.size(0), T)
        v_flat = valid_mask.float()
        if mean_only:
            out = (x.float() - mean_t) * v_flat
        else:
            std_t = std.view(N, 1, 1).expand(N, G, T).reshape(x.size(0), T)
            out = ((x.float() - mean_t) / (std_t + 1e-4)) * v_flat
        return out, mean, std

    def _forward_and_get_logits(
        self,
        model: torch.nn.Module,
        prompt_ids: torch.Tensor,
        completion_ids: torch.Tensor,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Return [1, comp_len, V] fp32 logits aligned to completion tokens."""
        full_ids = torch.cat([prompt_ids, completion_ids], dim=1)
        prompt_len = prompt_ids.shape[1]
        comp_len = completion_ids.shape[1]
        with torch.autocast(device_type="cuda", enabled=True):
            outputs = model(input_ids=full_ids, use_cache=False)
        # logits = outputs.logits[:, prompt_len - 1 : prompt_len - 1 + comp_len, :].float()
        # ↑ fp32 cast disabled to reduce [1, T, V] peak memory. Downstream consumers
        # may upcast smaller tensors (gt_lp / mean_X) if needed.
        logits = outputs.logits[:, prompt_len - 1 : prompt_len - 1 + comp_len, :]
        return torch.nan_to_num(logits, nan=0.0, posinf=1e4, neginf=-1e4)

    def _forward_and_get_gt_lp(
        self,
        model: torch.nn.Module,
        prompt_ids: torch.Tensor,
        completion_ids: torch.Tensor,
        *,
        reward_temp: float,
        V_min: int,
        gt_ids: torch.Tensor,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Memory-efficient forward + return ONLY gt log-prob.

        OPD/ExOPD signals (`eval_gt − base_gt`, `λ(eval_gt − tb_gt) − (base_gt − tb_gt)`)
        depend only on per-token gt log-probs — the rest of the full-V log_prob tensor
        produced by log_softmax is wasted. This helper does the log_softmax inside the
        function and releases the big tensors before returning, so consecutive forwards
        (base/eval/tb) don't accumulate [1, T, V] fp32 tensors in memory.

        Memory profile per call:
          - Transient peak inside: bf16 logits + fp32 log_prob for [1, T, V]
            (e.g., ~7GB for T=8192, V=152064).
          - Sustained after return: only [1, T] gt_lp (~64KB).
          - Across N sequential forwards, peaks DON'T accumulate.

        Returns:
          gt_lp: [1, T] fp32 — log P(gt) at sampled token, full-V-normalized.
        """
        full_ids = torch.cat([prompt_ids, completion_ids], dim=1)
        prompt_len = prompt_ids.shape[1]
        comp_len = completion_ids.shape[1]
        with torch.autocast(device_type="cuda", enabled=True):
            outputs = model(input_ids=full_ids, use_cache=False)
        # Slice + V_min clamp + sanitize in native dtype (typically bf16).
        logits = outputs.logits[:, prompt_len - 1 : prompt_len - 1 + comp_len, :]
        if logits.size(-1) != V_min:
            logits = logits[..., :V_min]
        logits = torch.nan_to_num(logits, nan=0.0, posinf=1e4, neginf=-1e4)

        # Full-V log_softmax — stays in the input dtype (bf16) to keep the [1, T, V]
        # peak small. PyTorch's log_softmax kernel still accumulates in fp32 internally
        # for numerical stability. Done INSIDE the function so the big tensor doesn't
        # escape to the caller.
        # log_prob = F.log_softmax(logits.float() / reward_temp, dim=-1)
        # ↑ original fp32 path; restore by un-commenting if precision regressions appear.
        log_prob = F.log_softmax(logits / reward_temp, dim=-1)
        del logits  # release [1, T, V] now that log_prob has the info

        # Single-position gather — the only thing OPD/ExOPD signals actually need.
        gt_lp = log_prob.gather(-1, gt_ids).squeeze(-1)
        del log_prob  # release [1, T, V] before return

        return gt_lp

    def _log_reward_summary(
        self,
        signals: torch.Tensor,
        mask: torch.Tensor,
        invalid: torch.Tensor,
        completion_mask: torch.Tensor,
    ) -> None:
        if not self.accelerator.is_main_process:
            return

        B = signals.size(0)
        valid_lens = [int(completion_mask[i].sum().item()) for i in range(B)]

        denom = mask.float().sum(dim=1).clamp(min=1.0)
        scalar = -(signals * mask.float()).sum(dim=1) / denom
        scalar = torch.where(invalid, torch.full_like(scalar, float('nan')), scalar)
        rewards_scalar = scalar.tolist()
        print(f"  valid_lens: {valid_lens}", flush=True)

        g = self.num_generations
        if g > 1 and len(rewards_scalar) % g == 0:
            means, stds = [], []
            for i in range(0, len(rewards_scalar), g):
                grp = [r for r in rewards_scalar[i:i + g] if not math.isnan(r)]
                if len(grp) >= 2:
                    m = sum(grp) / len(grp)
                    s = math.sqrt(sum((r - m) ** 2 for r in grp) / (len(grp) - 1))
                    means.append(f"{m:+.4f}")
                    stds.append(f"{s:.4f}")
                elif len(grp) == 1:
                    means.append(f"{grp[0]:+.4f}")
                    stds.append("0")
                else:
                    means.append("NaN")
                    stds.append("NaN")
            print(f"  group_mean: [{', '.join(means)}]", flush=True)
            print(f"  group_std:  [{', '.join(stds)}]", flush=True)
        else:
            print(f"  rewards:    {[('NaN' if math.isnan(r) else f'{r:.5f}') for r in rewards_scalar]}", flush=True)

        self._eta_step_count += 1
        now = time.time()
        if self._eta_start_time is None:
            self._eta_start_time = now
            print(f"  [ETA] step {self._eta_step_count}/{self.args.max_steps} | measuring...", flush=True)
        else:
            elapsed = now - self._eta_start_time
            sec_per_step = elapsed / (self._eta_step_count - 1)
            remaining = self.args.max_steps - self._eta_step_count
            eta_seconds = remaining * sec_per_step
            eta_h = int(eta_seconds // 3600)
            eta_m = int((eta_seconds % 3600) // 60)
            print(
                f"  [ETA] step {self._eta_step_count}/{self.args.max_steps}"
                f" | {sec_per_step:.0f}s/step"
                f" | {eta_h}h {eta_m}m remaining",
                flush=True,
            )

    def _compute_opd_rewards(
        self,
        prompts_text: list[str],
        completion_ids: torch.Tensor,
        completion_mask: torch.Tensor,
        solutions: list[str],
        teacher_prompts_text: Optional[list[str]] = None,
    ) -> dict:
        """Core OPD reward: per_token_signal = (eval_gt - base_gt) - E_base[eval_logp - base_logp]
                                              = (eval_gt - base_gt) + KL(base || eval).
        Returns dict with 'signals', 'mask', 'invalid'.

        teacher_prompts_text: prompts rendered with the TEACHER's own chat_template
        (opd_teacher_template). When given, takes precedence over the
        no_think_teacher strip; encoding still uses the student tokenizer
        (shared-vocab assumption)."""
        args = self.opd_args
        device = self.accelerator.device
        tokenizer = self.processing_class
        B = len(prompts_text)
        T_max = completion_ids.size(1)

        per_token_signal_list: list[Optional[torch.Tensor]] = []
        is_invalid_list: list[bool] = []

        base_model = self.model
        eval_model = self.opd_teacher_model if self.opd_teacher_model is not None else self.model

        with torch.no_grad():
            for idx in range(B):
                prompt_text = prompts_text[idx]
                comp_ids_row = completion_ids[idx]
                comp_mask_row = completion_mask[idx]

                # Every rank must run identical number of forwards (ZeRO-3 all-gathers).
                # Invalid rows fall back to a length-1 forward and get NaN'd downstream.
                is_invalid = False
                valid_len = comp_mask_row.sum().item()
                if valid_len <= 1:
                    is_invalid = True
                    valid_len = max(valid_len, 1)
                comp_tokens = comp_ids_row[:valid_len]
                if len(comp_tokens) == 0:
                    is_invalid = True
                    comp_tokens = comp_ids_row[:1]
                comp_tensor = comp_tokens.unsqueeze(0)

                prompt_encoded = tokenizer(
                    prompt_text, return_tensors="pt", add_special_tokens=False
                )
                prompt_ids = prompt_encoded["input_ids"].to(device)

                # Resolve the teacher prompt (teacher-template render or no_think
                # variant) BEFORE any forward so the helper can stream through base
                # then eval without holding the big fp32 [1, T, V] tensors between calls.
                if teacher_prompts_text is not None:
                    # opd_teacher_template: teacher's own chat_template rendering.
                    teacher_prompt_encoded = tokenizer(
                        teacher_prompts_text[idx], return_tensors="pt", add_special_tokens=False
                    )
                    teacher_prompt_ids = teacher_prompt_encoded["input_ids"].to(device)
                elif args.opd_no_think_mode and args.opd_no_think_teacher:
                    teacher_prompt_text = self._strip_nothink_block(prompt_text)
                    teacher_prompt_encoded = tokenizer(
                        teacher_prompt_text, return_tensors="pt", add_special_tokens=False
                    )
                    teacher_prompt_ids = teacher_prompt_encoded["input_ids"].to(device)
                else:
                    teacher_prompt_ids = prompt_ids

                reward_temp = self.temperature
                # V_min from configs (Qwen3 family: consistent across base/eval).
                V_min = min(
                    self.accelerator.unwrap_model(base_model).config.vocab_size,
                    self.accelerator.unwrap_model(eval_model).config.vocab_size,
                )
                gt_ids = comp_tensor.clamp(max=V_min - 1).unsqueeze(-1)

                # Two memory-efficient forwards: each releases its full-V tensors
                # before returning, so base_gt and eval_gt are the only survivors.
                base_gt = self._forward_and_get_gt_lp(
                    base_model, prompt_ids, comp_tensor,
                    reward_temp=reward_temp, V_min=V_min, gt_ids=gt_ids,
                )
                eval_gt = self._forward_and_get_gt_lp(
                    eval_model, teacher_prompt_ids, comp_tensor,
                    reward_temp=reward_temp, V_min=V_min, gt_ids=gt_ids,
                )

                per_token_signal = eval_gt - base_gt - args.opd_rewards_bias

                per_token_signal = torch.nan_to_num(
                    per_token_signal, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0
                ).detach().squeeze(0)

                if is_invalid:
                    per_token_signal_list.append(None)
                else:
                    per_token_signal_list.append(per_token_signal)
                is_invalid_list.append(is_invalid)

        signals_padded = torch.zeros(B, T_max, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
        signals_mask = torch.zeros(B, T_max, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
        for i, sig in enumerate(per_token_signal_list):
            if sig is None:
                continue
            L = min(sig.shape[0], T_max)
            signals_padded[i, :L] = sig[:L].to(torch.float32)
            signals_mask[i, :L] = True
        invalid = torch.tensor(is_invalid_list, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)

        self._log_reward_summary(signals_padded, signals_mask, invalid, completion_mask)

        return {
            "signals": signals_padded,
            "mask": signals_mask,
            "invalid": invalid,
        }

    def _generate_and_score_completions(
        self, inputs: list[dict[str, Union[torch.Tensor, Any]]]
    ) -> dict[str, Union[torch.Tensor, Any]]:
        """Override GRPO scoring: generate, then replace placeholder reward with OPD signals."""
        mode = "train" if self.model.training else "eval"
        args = self.opd_args

        solutions = [x.get("solution", "") for x in inputs]

        # Qwen3+DeepSpeed can produce NaN logits → multinomial sampling crash.
        def _sanitize_logits_hook(module, input, output):
            if hasattr(output, "logits") and output.logits is not None:
                output.logits = torch.nan_to_num(
                    output.logits, nan=0.0, posinf=1e4, neginf=-1e4
                )
            return output

        hook_handle = self.model.register_forward_hook(_sanitize_logits_hook)

        try:
            result = super()._generate_and_score_completions(inputs)
        finally:
            hook_handle.remove()

        # Pad to max_completion_length so cross-rank [B, T] gathers stay shape-aligned.
        T_local = result["completion_ids"].size(1)
        T_full = self.max_completion_length
        if T_local < T_full:
            pad_amt = T_full - T_local
            pad_id = self.processing_class.pad_token_id
            result["completion_ids"] = F.pad(result["completion_ids"], (0, pad_amt), value=pad_id)
            result["completion_mask"] = F.pad(result["completion_mask"], (0, pad_amt), value=0)
            if result.get("old_per_token_logps") is not None:
                result["old_per_token_logps"] = F.pad(
                    result["old_per_token_logps"], (0, pad_amt), value=0.0
                )
            # Token-level IS ratio is (B, T_local) and must be padded to match the
            # padded per_token_loss. Sequence-level is (B, 1) → broadcasts, leave it.
            # Pad with 1.0 (neutral); pad positions are masked by completion_mask anyway.
            isr = result.get("importance_sampling_ratio")
            if isr is not None and isr.size(1) == T_local:
                result["importance_sampling_ratio"] = F.pad(isr, (0, pad_amt), value=1.0)

        prompts_text = [
            maybe_apply_chat_template(example, self.processing_class)["prompt"]
            for example in inputs
        ]

        # opd_teacher_template: render teacher-side prompts with the teacher's own
        # chat_template (student/teacher templates may differ, e.g. Gemma4 31B-it vs E4B).
        teacher_prompts_text = None
        if self.opd_teacher_tokenizer is not None:
            teacher_prompts_text = [
                maybe_apply_chat_template(example, self.opd_teacher_tokenizer)["prompt"]
                for example in inputs
            ]

        reward_data = self._compute_opd_rewards(
            prompts_text,
            result["completion_ids"],
            result["completion_mask"],
            solutions,
            teacher_prompts_text=teacher_prompts_text,
        )

        signals_all = gather(reward_data["signals"])   # [total_B, T]
        mask_all = gather(reward_data["mask"])         # [total_B, T]
        invalid_mask = gather(reward_data["invalid"])  # [total_B]
        self._metrics[mode]["invalid/count"].append(float(invalid_mask.sum().item()))
        self._metrics[mode]["invalid/frac"].append(
            float(invalid_mask.float().mean().item())
        )

        process_slice = slice(
            self.accelerator.process_index * len(inputs),
            (self.accelerator.process_index + 1) * len(inputs),
        )

        G = self.num_generations
        total_B, T = signals_all.shape
        N = total_B // G

        sig_float = signals_all.float()
        mask_float = mask_all.float()

        # γ=0 (hardcoded): raw per-token signal, no future spread.
        rewards_t = sig_float * mask_float

        valid_mat = mask_all.bool() & (~invalid_mask).unsqueeze(1)
        valid_mat_f = valid_mat.float()
        rewards_t = rewards_t * valid_mat_f

        # Group normalize is computed for METRICS only (advantages stay raw).
        _, mean_g, std_g = self._group_normalize(
            rewards_t, valid_mat, N, G, T, mean_only=not self.scale_rewards
        )
        is_std_zero = torch.isclose(std_g, torch.zeros_like(std_g))
        step_std = std_g

        # disable_adv_norm hardcoded True: advantages = raw rewards.
        advantages = rewards_t
        advantages = advantages * args.opd_gen_loss_weight
        advantages = advantages * valid_mat_f

        rewards_log = (rewards_t.sum(dim=1) / valid_mat_f.sum(dim=1).clamp(min=1))
        rewards_log = torch.where(invalid_mask, torch.full_like(rewards_log, float('nan')), rewards_log)
        reward_metric_mean = mean_g.mean().item()
        reward_metric_std = std_g.mean().item()
        advantages_log = advantages.mean(dim=1)

        result["advantages"] = advantages[process_slice]
        local_invalid = invalid_mask[process_slice]
        result["completion_mask"][local_invalid] = 0

        self._metrics[mode]["reward"][-1] = reward_metric_mean
        self._metrics[mode]["reward_std"][-1] = reward_metric_std
        self._metrics[mode]["frac_reward_zero_std"][-1] = is_std_zero.float().mean().item()

        try:
            gathered_std = self.accelerator.gather(step_std.detach()).float()
            if gathered_std.numel() > 0:
                self._metrics[mode]["reward_std/per_group_min"].append(gathered_std.min().item())
                self._metrics[mode]["reward_std/per_group_max"].append(gathered_std.max().item())
                if gathered_std.numel() >= 10:
                    self._metrics[mode]["reward_std/per_group_p1"].append(
                        torch.quantile(gathered_std, 0.01).item()
                    )
                    self._metrics[mode]["reward_std/per_group_p10"].append(
                        torch.quantile(gathered_std, 0.10).item()
                    )
                    self._metrics[mode]["reward_std/per_group_p25"].append(
                        torch.quantile(gathered_std, 0.25).item()
                    )
        except Exception:
            pass

        valid_rewards = rewards_log[~torch.isnan(rewards_log)]
        if len(valid_rewards) > 0:
            self._metrics[mode]["rewards/opd_reward/mean"][-1] = valid_rewards.mean().item()
            self._metrics[mode]["rewards/opd_reward/std"][-1] = valid_rewards.std().item()
        else:
            self._metrics[mode]["rewards/opd_reward/mean"][-1] = 0.0
            self._metrics[mode]["rewards/opd_reward/std"][-1] = 0.0

        self._logs["advantages"].clear()
        self._logs["advantages"].extend(advantages_log.tolist())

        return result

"""Per-token training signal for on-policy distillation (EDITABLE).

The fixed pipeline samples a rollout from the student, then runs three frozen
forward passes over that rollout and hands you, for every sampled token, what
each model thinks of it.  Your job is to turn those numbers into the dense
per-token advantage the GRPO update is driven by.

Symbols used below (all log-probabilities, all at temperature `temperature`,
all normalised over the full vocabulary):

    S(t)   = log p_student(y_t | prompt, y_<t)     the student's own rollout
    T(t)   = log p_teacher(y_t | prompt, y_<t)     frozen reasoning-tuned teacher
    R(t)   = log p_reference(y_t | prompt, y_<t)   frozen model the teacher was tuned FROM

and the three expectations under the student's own next-token distribution,
truncated to the student's top-K columns (K is fixed by the harness):

    E[S](t) = sum_v p_student(v) * log p_student(v)
    E[T](t) = sum_v p_student(v) * log p_teacher(v)
    E[R](t) = sum_v p_student(v) * log p_reference(v)

What is fixed and NOT reachable from here: the rollout itself, the three
forward passes, the top-K gather, the PPO clip, the masking of padding and of
degenerate rollouts, the constant the signal is multiplied by before it enters
the loss, the optimizer, the schedule and the checkpoint that is saved.
"""
import torch


def compute_per_token_signal(
    student_lp: torch.Tensor,
    teacher_lp: torch.Tensor,
    teacher_base_lp: torch.Tensor,
    mean_student_lp: torch.Tensor,
    mean_teacher_lp: torch.Tensor,
    mean_teacher_base_lp: torch.Tensor,
    completion_mask: torch.Tensor,
    solutions: list,
    step: int,
    total_steps: int,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Return the dense per-token advantage for one batch of rollouts.

    Args:
        student_lp:           [B, T] float32, S(t).
        teacher_lp:           [B, T] float32, T(t).
        teacher_base_lp:      [B, T] float32, R(t).
        mean_student_lp:      [B, T] float32, E[S](t).
        mean_teacher_lp:      [B, T] float32, E[T](t).
        mean_teacher_base_lp: [B, T] float32, E[R](t).

                              padding and on every position of a rollout the
                              harness has already rejected.  Values at False
                              positions are zeros and are discarded afterwards,
                              so you never have to mask your output -- but you
                              DO have to respect the mask in any reduction you
                              take across tokens or across the batch.
        solutions:            list[str] of length B, the training set's own
                              reference answer for each prompt.  Training data,
                              not evaluation data.
        step:                 optimizer step index, 0-based.
        total_steps:          total optimizer steps in this run.

        [B, T] float tensor, same shape as `student_lp`.  Larger means "make
        this token more likely".  Non-finite entries are zeroed by the harness.
    """
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # EDITABLE REGION
    # OPD2 (Heo et al. 2026, arXiv:2607.15161; opd2_trainer.py:314-324).
    # type-18 signal with pre-centering always on (mean_ratio == 1).
    signal = (teacher_lp - teacher_base_lp) - (mean_teacher_lp - mean_teacher_base_lp)

    signal = torch.where(
        (signal * d_base) < 0, torch.zeros_like(signal), signal

    return signal
    # END EDITABLE REGION
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

delta_raw baseline — the pure RL-delta, the clean regime-2 anchor.

This is the raw teacher-minus-reference log-prob at the student's own sampled
token: T - R, where R is the teacher's OWN pre-RL base model (Qwen3-4B-Base) and
T is the RL-post-trained teacher (Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507).  It transfers the
CHANGE that reasoning tuning made to the teacher, and carries no absolute
teacher-vs-student comparison at all -- so, by regime-2's hypothesis, it should
help regardless of the teacher-student capability gap, and it must beat the
EM-FT null in every setting.

It is exactly the shipped starter body (`custom_template.py`), so it is the
zero-new-code anchor for the family: opd2 adds pre-centering and a sign gate on
top of this, exopd adds a lambda>1 mixture with the (S-R) term on top of this.
Contrast `opd` (pure T - S, no reference), which is the regime-1 (classic
distillation from a stronger teacher) control and is expected to lag at small
gaps -- see the task description.

Reference: the delta term of OPD2 (Heo et al. 2026, arXiv:2607.15161), i.e.
`opd2_trainer.py`'s `eval_gt - base_gt` before centering and gating.

baselines.name: Constant advantage / self-SFT
baselines.docstring:
NULL baseline — the declared null.  It must lose.

A constant signal of 1 on every sampled token satisfies the I/O contract while
carrying no information from the teacher or the reference at all.  Under the
fixed GRPO update a uniform positive advantage reduces to maximising the
log-likelihood of the student's own samples, i.e. on-policy self-SFT (entropy
minimisation on its own rollouts).

If this arm ever wins, the metric is rewarding "the student trained for a
while" rather than "the teacher's per-token signal transferred reasoning", and
the task is broken.  It is a declared baseline, not a one-off check, so every
future sweep re-runs it.
